title: Collective Opinion Dynamics in Structured LLM Populations
abstract: arXiv:2604.11312v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large Language Models are increasingly deployed as interacting agents in settings such as online platforms, recommendation systems, and multi-agent applications. Understanding the collective behaviors that emerge from their interactions is therefore increasingly crucial, especially as these behaviors may shape public opinion and contribute to polarization. In this work, we investigate how network structure and group composition shape the evolution of opinions in populations of LLM agents engaged in multi-round debates. We generate networks with controlled levels of homophily and varying group sizes, and perform ten independent runs per configuration. The results show that LLM agents exhibit patterns that are highly sensitive to network structure, relative group sizes, and to the model itself. translated_title: 结构化LLM群体中的集体舆论动态
translated_abstract: 大语言模型越来越多地被部署为在线平台、推荐系统和多智能体应用等场景中相互交互的智能体。因此，理解这些交互所产生的集体行为正变得日益重要，尤其是这些行为可能会塑造公众舆论并加剧观点极化。在这项工作中，我们研究了网络结构和群体构成如何塑造参与多轮辩论的LLM智能体群体中观点的演化过程。我们生成了具有可控同质性水平（homophily）和不同群体规模的网络，并对每种配置进行十次独立实验。结果表明，LLM智能体所呈现的行为模式对网络结构、相对群体规模以及模型本身高度敏感。我们强调，即使在LLM群体中，低同质性也通过增加跨群体互动的机会来促进观点收敛。
tldr: 该论文发现LLM智能体群体的观点动态对网络结构、相对群体规模和底层模型高度敏感，且低同质性网络通过增加跨群体互动机会能够有效促进观点收敛。
en_tdlr: This paper finds that collective opinion dynamics among LLM agent populations are highly sensitive to network structure, relative group sizes, and the underlying model, while low homophily facilitates opinion convergence by increasing cross-group interaction opportunities.
